messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream/generate in prod-us-west-2. Paging events up, tail stalls showing for streaming requests. p95 ~180ms -> 620ms, p99 ~2.9s -> 6.8s. Cache miss rate for prefix cache jumped from 4% -> 71% in last 12m. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/prod/latency/5566001234 :rotating_light:
Anna (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledge. Looking at live traces + request logs now. @Sam can you check if any model or prefix-hash rollout happened in the last deploy window?
Sam (eng-runtime): Checking deploy history... I see a config push 10:03 UTC that adjusted prefix-hash v2 parameters (salt rotation + namespace mapping). It targeted 20% of traffic initially. Might have scaled up.
Maria (eng-sre): Confirmed: prefix-hash rollout started at 10:02:47 UTC and increased to 60% by 10:11. That correlates with the start of the miss spike.
Leo (infra): We also had a KV bucket rekey job running for kvbucket-17 around 10:08 which could've caused transient misses if clients read different namespaces.
Jess (support): We're getting tickets: "generations timing out" from several customers, two flagged as P1s. They report long waits then 503s.
Mike (CS): Customer A (enterprise) reported timeouts for 10 minutes, said their users saw failed submits in prod. They're asking for ETA.
Anna (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) Roll back prefix-hash config to previous stable (undo rollout) 2) Force cache warmup for hot prefixes (task) 3) Enable fallback routing to older cache tier/model 4) Increase cache node pool temporarily. I'm going to try rollback first.
Sam (eng-runtime): Agreed. I'm prepping a rollback. Rolling the prefix-hash config back to v1 for the streaming route. Command: `infractl deploy-config --service=runtime --config=prefix-hash:v1 --region=us-west-2`
Anna (oncall): Executing now.
Anna (oncall): `infractl deploy-config --service=runtime --config=prefix-hash:v1 --region=us-west-2` -> job 5566001240 started.
deploy-bot: Job 5566001240: rollback prefix-hash -> SUCCESS on 80% of nodes, continuing rollout to remaining nodes.
Sam (eng-runtime): Good. Rolling back should stop new cache namespace mismatches. But we've already got a warmup deficit; hit rate might take a few minutes to recover.
Maria (eng-sre): While rollback in flight, I'm increasing cache TTL on the prefix cache to reduce churn: `cachectl set-ttl prefixcache 600s --region us-west-2`
Leo (infra): I'm scaling cache-nodes up by 25% in us-west-2 to absorb load: `k8s scale deployment/prefix-cache --replicas=15 --namespace=cache-prod`
Anna (oncall): Also enabling temporary fallback routing: route 10% of streaming requests to dedicated sdc-cache tier: `routingctl add-fallback --route=/v1/stream/generate --target=sdc-cache --weight=10`
Jess (support): Notifying affected customers. Draft message: "We are investigating an increase in request latency and timeouts, mitigation steps underway. We'll update in 15m." Sending now. :email:
Mike (CS): Customer A updated: they saw partial recovery, still some errors. Asking for root cause and ETA for full resolution.
Sam (eng-runtime): Live logs show many 404s from cache lookups with mismatched namespace keys. Example snippet:
```
[10:09:12 UTC] cache_get prefixcache: key="1234abcd:prefixv2:..." -> MISS (namespace mismatch)
[10:09:12 UTC] stream_req id=abc123 latency=0.12s backend_wait=5.8s
```
That lines up with hash namespace flip.
Maria (eng-sre): p99 tail traces show streaming stalls waiting on KV paged reads 2-3s longer than baseline. Paging queue depth increased ~4x.
Anna (oncall): Current status: rollback job succeeded fully at 10:14:05 UTC. Cache TTL increase and scale started. Fallback routing active. Early signal: p95 down to ~240ms, p99 down to ~3.8s and trending. Cache miss rate dropping from 71% -> 34% over last 3m.
Leo (infra): Cache node scale is up, new pods ready. Paging queue consumption stable but still above baseline.
Sam (eng-runtime): I'm kicking off a targeted cache warmup script for top 500 prefixes by traffic: `scripts/warmup_prefixes --top=500 --concurrency=40 --region=us-west-2`
Anna (oncall): Please add a runbook entry for warmup and TTL change. Also record rollback job id and timestamps for postmortem.
Maria (eng-sre): Noting impact window: 10:02:45 -> 10:16:00 UTC (approx). Marking as SLO partial breach for p99 during that window.
Jess (support): I've sent updates to all affected customers and created follow-ups for CS to share postmortem.
Mike (CS): Requesting a short summary to share: impact, mitigation, next steps.
Anna (oncall): Summary: prefix-hash config rollout changed namespace mapping causing cache key namespace mismatch and large cache miss spike -> increased paging and streaming tail latency -> customer timeouts. Mitigations: rollback prefix-hash (done), increased cache TTL, scaled cache nodes, enabled fallback routing, warmup script started. Estimating full recovery in ~10-15m from now.
Sam (eng-runtime): Will prepare a more detailed timeline and the config diff for the change (who/what/why).
Maria (eng-sre): Triage actions (owners): Sam -> produce config diff + deploy logs. Leo -> KV rekey job correlation and ensuring no leftover rekeys. Anna -> assemble timeline and handoff to next oncall. Jess/Mike -> customer comms + impact list.
Anna (oncall): Handoff note: I'll remain on the thread for 10m then hand to Maria for deep-dive. If p99 > 2s after 10:40 UTC escalate to oncall paging rota.
deploy-bot: Job 5566001240: postfix check -> all nodes report prefix-hash v1.
Maria (eng-sre): Taking over for post-incident investigation after 10:30 UTC. Please drop any additional logs or links here.
Anna (oncall): Thanks team. Good containment. Leaving handoff notes in incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/5566001234-doc. :white_check_mark:
